correctness.rationale: The finite six-vertex bidirected graph and complete multipath criterion are defined exactly. Two independent exhaustive constructions return the same 1817 augmented faces. A deterministic 835-pair matching has 146 critical nonempty cells, with acyclicity verified over every one of 6408 nonempty Hasse incidences. Signed gradient-path reductions give D3: Z^101 to Z^12 with nine unit Smith factors and D4: Z^32 to Z^101 exactly zero; direct original mod-two chain ranks (23,169,444,208) corroborate all Betti numbers. The resulting integral homology groups are Z^3,Z^92,Z^32 in degrees 2,3,4, with no torsion. One zero-cell and no critical one-cell prove simple connectivity and π2≅Z^3 by Hurewicz. No unsupported wedge decomposition is inferred.

value.rationale: The octahedron K_{2,2,2} is the smallest balanced complete-tripartite graph and an especially symmetric first three-part extension of bidirectional graph-complex theory. Its complete torsion-free integral homology in three distinct positive degrees and the nonzero π2 are nontrivial, natural exact invariants, not pre-existing table recomputations or mere Euler ranks. This identifies a concrete multipartite benchmark beyond bidirectional paths/cycles and provides a reproducible base case for larger graph families, without claiming a general theorem.
